```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)

movies <- read_csv("data/movies.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Data cleaning

```{r}
#| label: clean-movie-data
#| cache: true
movies_clean <- movies |>
  separate_longer_delim(genre, delim = ", ")

movies_gap <- movies_clean |>
  filter(tomatoMeter != 0, audienceScore != 0) |>
  mutate(gap = tomatoMeter - audienceScore) |>
  group_by(genre) |>
  summarize(mean_gap = mean(gap, na.rm = TRUE), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n >= 100) |>
  arrange(mean_gap)

movies_summary <- movies_gap
```

## Tomatometer Distribution

```{r}
#| label: tomatometer-histogram
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
ggplot(movies, aes(x = tomatoMeter)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "#F8766D", color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Tomatometer Scores",
    subtitle = "29,783 films",
    x = "Tomatometer Score",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

**Tomatometer:** Critic scores concentrate toward the high end. Zero scores require caution because missing ratings may be recorded as zero.

## Critic-Audience Gap by Genre

```{r}
#| label: genre-gap-chart
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7
movies_summary |>
  mutate(genre = fct_reorder(genre, mean_gap, .desc = TRUE)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_gap, y = genre)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4C78A8") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Average Critic-Audience Gap by Genre",
    subtitle = "Genres with at least 100 films; negative values favor audiences, positive values favor critics",
    x = "Average Gap (Critic - Audience)",
    y = "Genre"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

**Genre comparison:** Negative gaps favor audiences, while positive gaps favor critics. Filtering to genres with at least 100 observations reduces misleading results from tiny samples.

## Spider-Man Ratings

```{r}
#| label: spiderman-data
spiderman_titles <- c(
  "Spider-Man",
  "Spider-Man 2",
  "Spider-Man 3",
  "The Amazing Spider-Man",
  "The Amazing Spider-Man 2",
  "Spider-Man: Homecoming",
  "Spider-Man: Far From Home",
  "Spider-Man: No Way Home"
)

spiderman <- movies |>
  filter(title %in% spiderman_titles) |>
  mutate(actor = case_when(
    title %in% c("Spider-Man", "Spider-Man 2", "Spider-Man 3") ~ "Tobey Maguire",
    title %in% c("The Amazing Spider-Man", "The Amazing Spider-Man 2") ~ "Andrew Garfield",
    title %in% c("Spider-Man: Homecoming", "Spider-Man: Far From Home", "Spider-Man: No Way Home") ~ "Tom Holland",
  )) |>
  arrange(releaseDateTheaters) |>
  mutate(title = factor(title, levels = title))

spiderman_long <- spiderman |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(tomatoMeter, audienceScore),
    names_to = "rating",
    values_to = "score"
  ) |>
  mutate(rating = recode(rating,
    tomatoMeter = "Critics",
    audienceScore = "Audiences"
  ))
```

```{r}
#| label: spiderman-line-chart
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
ggplot(spiderman_long, aes(x = title, y = score, color = rating, group = rating)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 10)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Critics = "#008080", Audiences = "#F8766D")) +
  labs(
    title = "Spider-Man Ratings: Critics and Audiences Agree Most on Holland Films",
    subtitle = "Rotten Tomatoes critic and audience scores across eight live-action films",
    x = "Film",
    y = "Score",
    color = "Rating"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: spiderman-actor-averages
spiderman |>
  group_by(actor) |>
  summarize(
    `Average critic score` = mean(tomatoMeter, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Average audience score` = mean(audienceScore, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Average gap` = mean(tomatoMeter - audienceScore, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(factor(actor, levels = c("Tobey Maguire", "Andrew Garfield", "Tom Holland"))) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

**Spider-Man:** Critics favor Maguire's films more strongly than audiences. Garfield's films favor audiences. Holland's films show the strongest agreement between critics and audiences.
